title: Scenario manifest
description: The contract a scenario states about itself: which outcome it is expected to produce, how to break it when that outcome is an error, and the named checkpoints a caller can stop it at. This is the input format every runtime-harness task after this one consumes.

schema_version.description: Version of this manifest format. Pinned by const so a manifest authored for a later format is refused by tooling, not read under today's assumptions; ScenarioManifest.SupportedManifestSchemaVersion states the same number.

scenario.description: Name of the scenario this manifest describes, e.g. the stem of its *.commands.json file.

expected_outcome.description: Whether the scenario is expected to complete normally, to fail with a specific error, or to represent the game's pre-content 'loading' screen (no content is ever read for this last one). Stated as data, not inferred from whether a fault block is present.

content_root.description: A repository-relative directory to read content from instead of the production content/ tree — for a fixture scenario that needs a deliberately different content set (e.g. heroes with no contracts) rather than a broken one.

fault.description: How to break the game before running the scenario, and where. Legal only alongside expected_outcome: error.

expected_error_code.description: The error code a caller running this scenario to failure should observe. Required when expected_outcome is error.

checkpoints.description: Named points in the scenario's command sequence a caller can resolve and stop at.

after_command_id.description: Commands up to and including this id have run when the checkpoint is reached. 0 means before any command.
